question.leadin: Give the following about Spanish Florida.
question.text: The Spanish founded this city in Florida in 1565, making it America's oldest city.
question.clue: The 1763 Treaty of Paris ceded this city's colony, against which James Oglethorpe led a 1740 expedition.

swap.leadin: This conflict began due to a dispute over whether Native Americans should be driven out of Virginia.
swap.text: Name this 1676 rebellion against colonial governor William Berkeley. It collapsed after its namesake died of dysentery.
swap.clue: A target of this conflict who owned the Green Spring Plantation was William Berkeley.

question.text: While the route he took is under debate, this man was the first European to cross the Mississippi River, on whose banks he would perish due to fever.
question.clue: After he died of illness, his mission was continued by Luis de Moscoso Alvarado.

swap.text: This author of The Bloody Tenent of Persecution founded Rhode Island to be a place of religious freedom.
swap.clue: Earlier in his life, he chafed at Archbishop William Laud's strict control of Anglican Church doctrine, escaping with his wife Mary to Boston.

question.text: This body was the elected portion of the Virginia General Assembly, the legislative body of colonial Virginia.
question.clue: Distinguished members included Captain Francis West and Reverend William Wickham.

swap.text: The Battle of the Plains of Abraham was a part of this war, the American theater of the Seven Years' War. During this war, George Washington lost Fort Necessity.
swap.clue: Dissatisfaction with the result of this war led to Pontiac's Rebellion.

question.text: This Quaker founded a colony named for him in 1681, from which Delaware later split off.
question.clue: In an event depicted by a Benjamin West painting, this man expanded his holdings by signing treaties with the Lenape tribe after he was given a colony by Charles II.

swap.text: In a failed attempt to break the siege, British forces under James Dalyell planned a surprise ambush on Pontiac's forces in what became this battle. It resulted in the deaths of Dalyell along with sixty of his men and was fought near Parent's Creek.

question.leadin: Name these founders of early American colonies.
question.text: In 1732, this English philanthropist received a charter from George II to settle the colony of Georgia, making it not only a buffer against Spanish invasion but also a refuge for debtors.
question.clue: Earlier, this man led a Parliamentary committee on prison reform, which inspired him to found a haven for debtors.

swap.text: It was built after a surprise attack on a group of French soldiers led by commander Jumonville. English forces retreated to Great Meadows and went against Indian counsel to build this fort under the command of George Washington. For 15 points-name this Virginia fort which was taken by the French in 1754, damping English contention in the Ohio valley.
swap.clue: This battle, as well as an earlier incident in a nearby Glen, would prompt the dispatch of the Braddock expedition the following year into the Ohio River Valley.

question.leadin: Name these colonial acts passed by the hated British.
question.text: Passed by Parliament at the same time as the repeal of the Stamp Act, this 1766 act proclaimed Parliament's absolute authority to legislate for the colonies.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Horatio Nelson.
swap.text: In 1784, Nelson was sent to the area near Antigua to enforce these acts, which restricted foreign vessels from trading with England or its colonies.
swap.clue: Repealed officially in 1849, they were accompanied by the Staple Act and targeted items subject to "enumeration."

question.text: The Fundamental Agreement of the New Haven Colony created a court of 16 people with this title, who were "chosen out of the church members." Elected representatives in colonial Virginia also had this title.

swap.leadin: At this meeting, Hendrick Theyanoguin allowed the trading village of Shamokin to be ceded to Pennsylvania.
swap.text: Name this 1754 meeting. Its "Plan of Union" was proposed by Benjamin Franklin, who promoted it with his "Join, or Die" cartoon.
swap.clue: Peter Wraxall served as its chronicler, repeatedly referencing the "Fire of Friendship".

question.leadin: These three words appear underneath the image of a snake cut into eight segments.
question.text: What three words appear under that image in a 1754 political cartoon created to promote unity during the French and Indian War?
question.clue: This three word phrase which appears in a 1754 political cartoon designed by Ben Franklin, which featured a snake representing the American colonies cut into eighths. Franklin's use of the phrase was intended to promote the unity of the colonies.

swap.text: One of the propaganda highlights of the Long March was the capture of one of these structures in Luding County, Sichuan ("SUCH-wahn"). The Japanese invasion of China proper began with a skirmish at one of these structures in Beijing named after Marco Polo.
swap.answerHtml: bridges [or qiao; accept Battle of Luding Bridge; accept Marco Polo Bridge Incident]
swap.clue: Allied forces attempted to capture these places at Nijmegen and Arnhem during Operation Market Garden.

question.leadin: Jeremiah Gridley argued for the legality of these instruments, which were introduced to enforce the Acts of Trade, and his argument was upheld by Chief Justice Thomas Hutchinson.
question.text: Name these general search warrants, which gave customs officers legal authority to inspect ships and homes at will, and were thus quite controversial in colonial America.

swap.leadin: Name these proprietary founders of colonies in the New World.
swap.text: After this man funded the failed Popham Colony, he was given a grant with his friend John Mason, which they split at the Piscataqua River. Despite the fact that he never set foot in North America, this man is called the "father of English colonization" because he thusly founded the province of Maine.
swap.clue: This owner of the Plymouth Council who was given several land grants and founded the Popham or Sagadahoc settlement in 1606. Though he never set foot in America, his heirs spent the 17th century litigating his claims.

question.text: The revolt was crushed at this two-hour battle, where the Regulators told Tryon to "fire and be damned" after being told to lay down their arms.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a colonial Indian War.
swap.text: One source on the war is the journal and narrative history Of Plimoth Plantation, written by this long-time governor of the Plymouth Colony.
swap.clue: His most notable work chronicles the changing of the name of Mount Wallaston to Merry Mountain.
